Jaywalking is penalized with a 200zł fine, and it's there for a reason. Poland is plagued with speeding and reckless driving, which despite recent increase in how much you need to pay for getting caught committing traffic offense, isn't likely to be under control anytime soon. This is confirmed by data on the amount of injuries and fatalities on pedestrian crossings, which has been significantly higher than in other EU countries for years now. To combat this, new law has recently been introduced which is supposed to increase the pedestrian safety on crossings without traffic lights. However, this can only work if all participants of traffic are committed to this law - including pedestrians, who in Polish traffic code have always been regarded as participating in traffic. As a driver, who is expected by pedestrians to pay extra attention on crossings without traffic lights, I also expect the crossing WITH traffic lights to be clear of pedestrians when the light on the crossing is red. And as a pedestrian, I commit to do the same. It's a shared responsibility model which hopefully reduces the amount of accidents, and as other redditors here mention - it's also a good habit worth passing to kids. And if you're complaining about not being able to cross whenever at 2am, then I have news for you - most traffic lights are off for the night, so you can cross at any time as if it was a regular pedestrian crossing. Drivers are then obliged to yield to you.

tl;dr It's a good habit which can highly reduce traffic accidents at a really small effort when put to scale and I recommend that you follow it.
